citations.quote: How many assists will each player make?

Subject to the settlement exceptions below, this market resolves to Yes if Rudy Gobert records 2 or more Assists in the NBA game between New York and Minnesota originally scheduled for November 19, 2026 at 8:00 PM ET, including any overtime periods. Otherwise, it resolves to No. The Underlying is the official Assists credited to the specified player in that game. The Source Agency is NBA.com and its official Stats platform (nba.com/stats). If unavailable, the Exchange may use, in hierarchical order, (i) ESPN and (ii) ABC, NBC, Amazon Prime Video, or the official broadcast or streaming partner of the game.

If the player records no playing time in the Source Agency's official box score for any reason, the Contract resolves to the last fair price determined in the sole discretion of the Exchange. If the player appears, settlement uses the actual credited Assists, regardless of playing time or subsequent removal from the game.

If the game is postponed before it begins, the Contract remains open and active and expires one hour after the Source Agency reports the official final statistics of the rescheduled game. If the game is not made up by the final scheduled day of the applicable NBA regular season or postseason round, the Contract resolves to the last fair price determined in the sole discretion of the Exchange. If postponed by more than two weeks, the Exchange may resolve the Contract to the last fair price in its sole discretion under Rule 7.2. If the game is officially cancelled with no result declared and no make-up game scheduled, the Contract resolves to the last fair price determined in the sole discretion of the Exchange. If a suspended game is later completed, settlement uses the player's cumulative recorded Assists following completion.

Except as otherwise provided by these settlement exceptions, the Contract expires one hour after official final statistics are available from the Source Agency. Revisions after expiration do not affect settlement. Before settlement, the Exchange may initiate the Market Outcome Review Process under Rule 7.1. If an Expiration Value cannot be determined on the Expiration Date in a scenario not described above, the Exchange may determine payouts pursuant to Rule 7.1. View the [full rules](https://assets.gemini.com/predictions/terms_and_conditions/Terms_and_Conditions_NBA_Player_Assists_Class_76239ffa-aa99-438c-8704-db71de2d2363.pdf).

workbook_conflicts: Scale: the README specifies 1-5 per category; the workbook uses 1-3. This prototype uses the workbook's 1-3 scale and 4-12 totals.

Markets!B formula =IF(I>=9,"High",IF(I>=7,"Medium","Low")) ignores the Framework overrides, and SUM() treats a blank score as 0, so an incomplete row shows as Low. The code reports incomplete ratings instead.
Volume column mixes bases: rows 2-4 are event totals from the Gemini API, rows 5-6 are 24h figures from CoinRithm, while Agent rule 4 is written for 24h volume.
Override 'any 3 in Ambiguity or Source -> at least Medium' only changes the result at a raw total of 6 (for example 3+1+1+1); at 7 or more the total is already Medium.
Override 'High (3) in Liquidity -> never trade more than top-of-book' is a trading rule. Verity places no trades, so it becomes a note that the price is an unreliable signal.
Agent action column uses trading verbs (Proceed, Proceed small size). They are mapped to research actions: Low -> no_further_research, Medium -> investigate, High -> flag_for_human_review.
